newsitem.title: USA: Ill. suburban airport plan on shaky ground - paper.
newsitem.headline: Ill. suburban airport plan on shaky ground - paper.

text.p: A city-commissioned report says planning for a third major airport in the far south suburbs of Chicago has overestimated likely federal funding and understimated costs, Chicago Sun-Times reported Wednesday.
The Fullerton & Friar Inc report noted that investors in the municipal bond market "are generally not oriented toward "taking a flyer on a long-shot investment'," the Sun-Times reported.
The Chicago aviation department commissioned the report from St. Petersburg, Florida-based Fullerton at the urging of the Chicagoland Chamber of Commerce, the Sun-Times reported.

The report said state officials anticipate federal funding of 50 percent to 72 percent of the project, but major projects would be fortunate to receive funding for 15 percent to 20 percent of the cost, the Sun-Times reported.
Illinois Transportation Secretary Kirk Brown told the Sun-Times that the funding assumptions were reasonable and argued that the report's findings were inaccurate.
Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar, a Republican, has supported building a third major airport in the suburban metropolitan area, while Chicago Mayor Richard Daley proposed to build one within the city limits.

United Airlines and American Airlines have made major additions to their extensive hubs at O'Hare International Airport in recent years and have said they will not use or support a third regional airport in the south suburbs.
Illinois transportation department has estimated that the initial facility could cost $342 million to $473 million, requiring up to $225 million of federal money, the Sun-Times reported.
